## Market Size

- **Category:** individual/personal task management, a sub-segment of the broader productivity-management software market. (Grand View Research; Fortune Business Insights — categories, not figures.)
- **Reported figures — `unverified`, verify before quoting:**
  - Grand View Research reportedly sizes global *productivity management software* at ~USD 61.65B (2023), CAGR ~14% to 2030.
  - Fortune Business Insights reportedly sizes the narrower *task management software* market at ~USD 5B (2023), CAGR ~14–15%.
  - Statista tracks consumer task-app downloads/revenue separately (figures not recalled reliably).
- **SAM / SOM:** `unknown`. Requires a defined segment (knowledge workers 25–45 + freelancers) × ARPU assumption. No number produced — fabricating one would violate the no-fabrication rule.
- **Demand context (unverified):** normalization of remote/hybrid work and mobile productivity adoption are cited as tailwinds by industry reports.
- **Verify with:** `"productivity management software market size 2024 Grand View Research"`, `"task management software market size Fortune Business Insights 2024"`, `"personal productivity app revenue Statista 2024"`.

## Competitor

Direct and adjacent named products (pricing `unverified`, verify — pricing changes frequently):

- **Todoist** (Doist) — cross-platform task manager; natural-language quick add; Pro ~$4–5/mo annual. Prioritization: manual labels/filters + Upcoming. Positioning: simplicity + power.
- **TickTick** — to-do + calendar + habits + Pomodoro + Eisenhower matrix; Premium ~$35.99/yr. Notable built-in priority views.
- **Things 3** (Cultured Code) — Apple-only, **one-time purchase** (~$9.99 iOS / $49.99 Mac). Manual prioritization; design-led; signals buyer resistance to subscriptions.
- **Microsoft To Do / Google Tasks** — free, bundled with OS/work ecosystems; prioritization weak or invisible; cap paid willingness-to-pay.
- **Notion** — docs + databases; task management is one use case; ~$10/mo; high setup cost.
- **Motion / Reclaim.ai / Akiflow / Sunsama** — AI/auto-scheduling niche; Motion ~$34/mo, Sunsama ~$20/mo, Reclaim ~$8–10/mo. **Closest on "automatic prioritization"** but pricey and/or calendar-scheduling-centric.
- **Contract alternatives (not products):** paper lists, notes apps, calendar-only, email-to-self.

## Positioning

- **Claimed differentiation (from product definition):** simplicity + *trustworthy* auto-prioritization for individuals — an auto-ranked Today list, not another sortable inbox.
- **Whitespace hypothesis (`hypothesis`, not evidence):** mass-market simple tools (Todoist, TickTick, Microsoft/Google) leave prioritization manual; AI schedulers (Motion, Reclaim, Sunsama) are powerful but expensive/complex. A low-friction, **explanation-first** auto-ranked list for individuals is plausibly underserved.
- **Trust is the wedge:** "why this rank" explainability + one-tap manual override directly targets the top technical risk (AI ranking ≠ user intent) and the override-rate guardrail (<30%).
- **Deliberate boundaries:** no team/Gantt/resource features → explicitly excludes Asana, Monday.com, Jira and their enterprise buyers.
- **Positioning risks:**
  - Crowded category; differentiation claim is unvalidated.
  - Free ecosystem incumbents (Microsoft, Google) cap paid conversion.
  - One-time-purchase precedent (Things) signals subscription resistance for personal tools.
- **Needs research:** override-rate benchmark for trust; willingness-to-pay for priority/analytics depth; competitive positioning test (is "trustworthy auto-prioritization" actually perceived as a gap by target users?).
